overall: The AG found a subcommittee of the Planning Board, formed at a joint meeting, was a public body that violated the Open Meeting Law by holding two unposted meetings; it ordered future compliance and reconstructed minutes.

allegations.summary: A subcommittee formed at a joint board meeting allegedly held two meetings (January 19 and 29) without posting any notice.
allegations.key_passage: The group did not post notice of either meeting.

allegations.summary: The Board contended the working group was a focus group, not a public body, because it did not intend to create a subcommittee. The AG rejected this and found it subject to the law.
allegations.key_passage: Based on the totality of the evidence reviewed, we find that the group is a subcommittee within the scope of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Create minutes for all previous group meetings to the best of its ability, using available means including attendees' memories and notes, within 60 days of receipt of the letter
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Further, we order the Board to create minutes for all previous group meetings to the best of its ability, through whatever means are available, including the memories and individual notations of the attendees.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
